target.title: fix: cloud-worker results are lost when the box dies before reconciliation
target.body:
Related: #110224 (phase 1 of 3)

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves the data-loss half of #110224: a cloud-worker turn's file result only existed on the leased box until a clean workspace apply succeeded. If inbound reconciliation failed (real local divergence) and the box then died — or the Gateway restarted and its recovery sweep found the environment gone — the unaccepted result was abandoned and the placement force-failed, permanently losing the turn's work. Observed live during a cloud-workers stress test (full incident log in #110224).

## Why This Change Was Made

Stage-first reconciliation: when a worker result is pulled, the complete result tree is committed as a durable Git ref in the session workspace repo (`refs/openclaw/worker-results/<claim>`, with a crash-safe candidate ref during construction) before any apply is attempted, and recorded on the pending-result fence row (new nullable `staged_result_ref` column, state schema v5, additive migration). Apply and every retry then run from the staged tree as a purely local operation; the recovery sweep skips the tunnel entirely when a staged ref exists. Recovery semantics change accordingly: an unaccepted fence with a staged ref must never be destroyed by environment lifecycle — the environment can be reclaimed while the fence and placement stay alive until the local apply is durably accepted. Only legacy fences without a staged ref keep the old abandon path. Staged refs are deleted on acceptance or explicit abandonment; ref construction validates claim ids (`[A-Za-z0-9-]+`) and fails closed; ordering is candidate apply → quiescence/fence checks → canonical ref publish → SQLite pointer, so a crash at any step leaves a recoverable state. Object retention after ref deletion matches the existing managed-worktree snapshot pattern (`refs/openclaw/snapshots/*`).

Non-goals (later phases per #110224): conflict resolution policy, turn-claim release semantics, chat error copy, UI affordances.

Maintainer rulings for this PR: keep the state schema at `main + 1` (v5); the rollback consequence is deliberately accepted. Complete-tree staging and object-store retention parity with managed-worktree snapshots are also accepted design decisions.

## User Impact

A dead or reclaimed cloud box can no longer lose a finished turn's file changes: the result is already safe on the Gateway and is applied or retried locally. Gateway restarts preserve pending results instead of force-failing their placements.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/ src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts` — 447 tests green (89 + 358 across shards), including: staging order (ref before apply), crash-gap adoption of canonical refs, dead-environment recovery applying from the staged ref without a tunnel, divergence keeping fence + placement alive, ref cleanup on accept, hostile git-hook neutralization, and the v4→v5 migration.
- Remote `pnpm check:changed` (Blacksmith Testbox): exit 0 (typecheck, lint, format, policy guards, import cycles).
- Structured autoreview (codex, gpt-5.6-sol): accepted findings fixed (ref-name validation, staging/finalization race reordering, candidate-ref leak); final run clean. Two rejected-by-owner suggestions documented inline (object-store retention parity with worktree snapshots; complete-tree vs delta storage is the requested contract).

### Real recovery proof

Exact head `a9d37cdda82c3bb1ce5092c9609a609366f31245` was built and run through an isolated real Gateway → bundled Crabbox provider → AWS worker path. The model side used the deterministic local QA provider; provisioning, bundle install, SSH/tunnel, worker runtime, workspace transfer, durable staging, lease loss, Gateway restart, and recovery were production paths.

The proof injected one persistence-boundary failure with an isolated SQLite trigger: reject the first `workspace_accepted_at_ms` update after the canonical staged Git ref was published. This models the crash window without modifying production code. It then stopped the actual AWS lease before restarting the Gateway.

```text
provider: aws
lease: cbx_f8b8fd6f4912 (stopped before Gateway restart; cleaned up)
pending before restart: staged_result_ref present, workspace_accepted_at_ms null
worker result before restart sha256: e0b584a31c3f16c59b04d9e00d0c4421618f0ad633ededdefa3e052fc401eb2c
worker result after restart sha256:  e0b584a31c3f16c59b04d9e00d0c4421618f0ad633ededdefa3e052fc401eb2c
pending rows after restart: 0
placement after restart: reclaimed
turn claim after restart: null
recovery_error after restart: null
staged Git ref after restart: absent
```

The first harness attempt reached an attached AWS worker but selected an empty side-database path before starting a turn; it failed during trigger installation and cleaned up its lease. The corrected run above used the Gateway's canonical `state/openclaw.sqlite` path and completed end to end.
